_note: Draft English rendering of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 3, drafted against the JA (not the biblical Hebrew) for reverse-translatability in the Tafsir reader. Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted, including 3:1 (אף כי → 'verily'), 3:3 (דנא ב → 'approach'), 3:8 (לרוח היום → 'with the movement of the day'), 3:16-17 (עצבון → 'toil', not 'pain'), 3:22 (לעולם → 'forever'). Calibration batch.

translations.1: And the serpent became wiser than every living creature of the wilderness which God had created. And he said to the woman: 'Verily — did God say, "You shall not eat from any tree of the garden"?'
translations.2: And she said to him: 'From the fruit of the trees of the garden we may eat;
translations.3: but from the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God said: "Do not eat from it, and do not approach it, lest you die."'
translations.4: And he said to her: 'You shall not surely die;
translations.5: for God knows that on the day you eat from it, your eyes will burst open, and you will become like the angels — knowing good and evil in greater measure.'
translations.6: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for eating and pleasing in appearance, and an object of yearning for the intellect — she took from its fruit and ate; and she gave her husband too with her, and he ate.
translations.7: And the eyes of the two of them burst open, and they knew that they were naked; and they stitched together from the leaves of the fig, and made for themselves loincloths.
translations.8: And they heard the voice of God passing through the garden gently, with the movement of the day; and Adam and his wife hid themselves out of shame, from before God, among the trees of the garden.
translations.9: And God called to Adam, and said to him by way of confirming: 'Where are you?'
translations.10: He said: 'I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, since I am naked; and so I hid.'
translations.11: He said: 'Who told you that you are naked? Is it from the tree which I commanded you not to eat from, that you have eaten?'
translations.12: Adam said: 'The woman whom You set with me — she gave me of the tree, and so I ate.'
translations.13: And God said to the woman: 'What is this that you have done?' She said: 'The serpent led me astray, and so I ate.'
translations.14: And God said to the serpent: 'Since you did this knowingly, you are cursed from among all the beasts and from among all the wild creatures of the wilderness. Upon your chest you shall travel, and dust you shall eat, all the days of your life.
translations.15: And enmity shall I set between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring; he shall crush you on the head, and you shall bite him on the heel.'
translations.16: And He said to the woman: 'I shall greatly increase your toil and your pregnancy; in toil shall you bear children; and toward your husband shall be your inclination, and he shall rule over you.'
translations.17: And He said to Adam: 'Since you accepted the voice of your wife, and ate from the tree which I commanded you, saying, "You shall not eat from it" — cursed is the earth on your account; in toil shall you eat from it, all the days of your life.
translations.18: And thorn and thistle shall it cause to grow for you; and you shall eat the herbage of the wilderness.
translations.19: By the sweat of your face shall you eat food, until your return to the earth from which you were taken; for you are dust, and to dust you shall return.'
translations.20: And Adam called the name of his wife Eve, because she was to be the mother of every speaking creature.
translations.21: And God made for Adam and his wife body-garments, and clothed the two of them.
translations.22: Then God said: 'Behold, Adam has become like one of Us in the knowledge of good and evil; and now — lest he stretch out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever' —
translations.23: And God expelled him from the garden of Eden, to till the earth from which he had been taken.
translations.24: And when Adam had been expelled, He settled east of the garden of Eden angels, and the flash of a turning sword — that they might guard the path of the tree of life.
